"I want others to hear my story and to know help is out there." By Georgie Docker North West Published 1 hour ago A mental health campaigner said they were seconds away from taking their own life before being saved by a plotline in a soap opera. John Junior, 37, from Wythenshawe, in Greater Manchester, had been suffering with depression since the age of 14. But after the sudden death of their father in 2018, the then-IT worker said they hit rock bottom. During lockdown in 2020, John was contemplating taking their own life when a Hollyoaks storyline stopped them in their tracks. "I seconds away from ending my life," John recalled. "I had Hollyoaks on in the background and I turned round to watch the scene. "There was a moment when a character was told her partner had taken his own life. "Something happened to me and it gave me enough time to think beyond what I was about to do. "I wouldn't be here today if it wasn't for Hollyoaks." Ahead of World Suicide Prevention Day 2026, on 10 September, John said now they want to share their experience to encourage others to speak out. title: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations

evidence_packet.title: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations
evidence_packet.lead: Ambrose Barlow was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death in 1641
evidence_packet.summary: Ambrose Barlow was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death in 1641
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The skull of a saint that was discovered during renovations - BBC News Image caption, The skull of St Ambrose Barlow is on display at Wardley Hall By Jen Dale North West Published 6 September 2026 On 25 April 1641, Ambrose Barlow celebrated a secret Easter Sunday mass at Morleys Hall near Astley in Greater Manchester. But, by the end of the service, the building had been surrounded by a 400-strong armed group led by a local vicar. "King Charles I issued a decree stating that all Catholic priests must leave within a month...and if they didn't, they would face the consequences of treason," said the Right Reverend John Arnold, the Bishop of Salford. King Charles I wanted to prove that he supported the Protestant faith while keeping his political enemies at bay as parliament were suspicious of his Catholic wife. The congregation urged Ambrose Barlow to hide but Arnold said he refused and instead ordered the doors to be opened and surrendered peacefully. "He didn't make any attempt to avoid arrest," said Arnold. "He was really concerned for the safety of the people attending mass - about 150 of them." Image source, Diocese of Salford Image caption, The Right Reverend John Arnold said records showed Ambrose Barlow had a "good sense of humour" and was "very mild in his character" He was taken to Lancaster Castle where he was imprisoned. After four months, he was put on trial, charged with being a priest. He was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death. "On 10 September, which is now his feast day, he was hung, drawn, and quartered," said Arnold. "And his skull was put on a pike as a demonstration to people that this is what happens if you are a Catholic." It was a warning to all who refused to conform to the state religion. Beth Abbi Graham Stringer took over leadership of Manchester Council from 1984 with Pat as his deputy and the two men went on a mission to make the Village a safe space. But as Pat Karney says in the latest episode of the Mancunian Way podcast , the 1980s were “very dark times” for anyone He describes a “low level of paranoia” among the community with most fearing attacks and persecution. “You basically had to hide your sexuality,” he says “The culture was anti-gay. You're always frightened about going out. There was no shiny gay village saying ‘gay bars’. They were all very secretive and hidden away. Windows were deliberately either curtained or clouded.” In the mid-1980s, Mancunians were living alongside a police force led by a chief constable heavily influenced by his Christian faith who once claimed to be “used by God” to speak out on moral issues. His remains were hidden in Japanese knotweed on the edge of playing fields used by Broughton Cricket and Rugby Club in Sal But the truth was his life had ebbed away weeks earlier. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Blackpool Mum's fight for son's medical records after tragic E.coli death following Blackpool beach swim Rachael Bell believes her son Matthew's death in 1997 may have been linked to sewage at a beach near Blackpool, and spent nearly three decades try A Lancashire mother who suspects her young son's death almost 30 years ago may have been connected to sewage contamination at a beach near Blackpool has opened up about her battle to access his medical records Rachael Bell, 61, revealed she spent decades carrying the burden of guilt over the death of her beloved son Matthew, who passed away aged just under four in 1997. Matthew initially experienced diarrhoea and severe stomach cramps before his condition became critical He was diagnosed with E. coli O157, amongst the most hazardous strains of the bacteria, and subsequently developed haemolytic uraemic syndrome, a rare complication that can result in kidney failure Matthew's younger brother Tom also fell ill with the same infection but fortunately made a full recovery Matthew's health worsened and he was transferred to Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool . Following several harrowing weeks, he slipped into a coma and was relocated to intensive care before his tragic death towards the end of October, reports Lancs Live

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport 'She was like a sister, but it was cancer which brought us closer together again' Natalie Luxton said her breast cancer diagnosis brought her 'closer together' with a childhood neighbour and friend News Emily Parker Shopping Writer 17:36, 06 Natalie Luxton had been preparing to celebrate her husband's birthday with a trip to Centre Parcs when she noticed a lump on her right side. She assumed it would be nothing but as she had the day off work decided to get it checked The 39-year-old, from Stockport , had a biopsy but left assuming she would get the all-clear. In March, this year, she got a call back to receive her results and when she heard it was breast cancer, she was left feeling as though her world was falling apart "I'm not someone who really worries so I was convinced in my head that it wasn't cancer," recalls Natalie. "I've heard mixed stories where people have gone back in and had the results and it wasn't. So the fact we did have to go back didn't worry me too much "We sat down and the consultant said talk me through what you know up to now. So I started talking through the process up to that point and he just said, 'okay, I'm sorry to tell you you've got breast cancer' View 6 Images Natalie Luxton with her husband (Image: Supplied)

evidence_packet.summary: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe. Beth Abbi Graham Stringer took over leadership of Manchester Council from 1984 with Pat as his deputy and the two men went on a mission to make the Village a safe space. But as Pat Karney says in the latest episode of the Mancunian Way podcast , the 1980s were “very dark times” for anyone He describes a “low level of paranoia” among the community with most fearing attacks and persecution. “You basically had to hide your sexuality,” he says “The culture was anti-gay. You're always frightened about going out. There was no shiny gay village saying ‘gay bars’. They were all very secretive and hidden away. Windows were deliberately either curtained or clouded.” In the mid-1980s, Mancunians were living alongside a police force led by a chief constable heavily influenced by his Christian faith who once claimed to be “used by God” to speak out on moral issues. James Anderton had the support of Margaret Thatcher and used his position to ord View 7 Images Sir James Anderton was Greater Manchester Police's chief constable at the time

evidence_packet.summary: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime r
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:22, 06 Sep 2026 Two years ago Mohammed Fahir Amaaz, together with his brother and mother who was sporting a black eye, appeared at a press conference in a fancy suite at Manchester's Midland Hotel They didn't speak a word but they looked suitably solemn as their lawyer held them up to be a virtuous pro-police family - some of them serving police officers - who had been the victim of shocking and unprovoked police brutality at Manchester Airport six days earlier Not only that but they were then subjected to a 'deliberate attempt to smear them' by someone inside GMP That was because, two days before the press conference, the Manchester Evening News obtained and then published CCTV footage which provided some context to the by then infamous violence which erupted in the pay station at Terminal 2 at the airport It was a clip that gave perspective to earlier mobile phone footage of an armed police officer kicking the face of Amaaz as he lay prone and motionless on the ground

title: Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?

evidence_packet.title: Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble... but he was not choosing his friends wisely" View 7 Images Julius Matera was 43 when he died News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:08, 06 Sep 2026 Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was pronounced dead by paramedics at ten minutes past noon on December 8, 2023. His remains were hidden in Japanese knotweed on the edge of playing fields used by Broughton Cricket and Rugby Club in Sal But the truth was his life had ebbed away weeks earlier. He suffered catastrophic blood loss on the night of October 13 and 14 that year Known as Julius, he had been reported missing on October 24, but by then he had already been dead a week. It was 56 days later and in dramatic fashion that his body was found But an explosive inquest at Bolton coroners court heard how a wall of silence has meant his family have been denied justice in what they believe is a case of murder View 7 Images Julius was described as "quite literally a gentle man"

Do you understand what's happening?" Business Secretary and Stalybridge and Hyde MP Jonathan Reynolds was asked what he made of the Reform politician's tweet. He told Sky News's Sunday Morning programme: "Pretty straightforward racism, isn't it?" Mr Reynolds added that the potential Labour candidate had 'spent decades in this country' and made a 'huge contribution to her local community'. He was rushed to Royal Preston Hospital with severe head injuries, a court heard But he died later on October 11 last year, Lancs Live reports . Foden has now been sentenced for drug driving in Preston Magistrates' Court In an emotional statement read in court, Rhodes' loved ones said: "There isn't a day we don't think about him." The court heard an investigation had found Foden was not responsible for the accident A conclusion of misadventure was recorded following an earlier inquest at Blackpool Coroners' Court. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Blackpool Mum's fight for son's medical records after tragic E.coli death following Blackpool beach swim Rachael Bell believes her son Matthew's death in 1997 may have been linked to sewage at a beach near Blackpool, and spent nearly three decades try A Lancashire mother who suspects her young son's death almost 30 years ago may have been connected to sewage contamination at a beach near Blackpool has opened up about her battle to access his medical records Rachael Bell, 61, revealed she spent decades carrying the burden of guilt over the death of her beloved son Matthew, who passed away aged just under four in 1997. Matthew initially experienced diarrhoea and severe stomach cramps before his condition became critical He was diagnosed with E. coli O157, amongst the most hazardous strains of the bacteria, and subsequently developed haemolytic uraemic syndrome, a rare complication that can result in kidney failure Matthew's younger brother Tom also fell ill with the same infection but fortunately made a full recovery Matthew's health worsened and he was transferred to Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool . Following several harrowing weeks, he slipped into a coma and was relocated to intensive care before his tragic death towards the end of October, reports Lancs Live

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS Sweltering, under strain and facing a 'real problem': An extreme summer in our NHS Doctors say they have faced increased demand, soaring temperatures and no respite from the winter View 9 Images Hospitals have experienced soaring heat this summer Comments News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:07, 07 Sep 2026 For some of us, it has been a pleasure. For others it has seemed relentless In NHS buildings across Greater Manchester and beyond, the scorching summer truly left its mark. The UK has experienced record-breaking heat this summer Five heatwaves have blasted the country, leaving more than two-thirds of England and all of Wales in drought. Although the North West is not in drought, Greater Manchester has still basked in prolonged spells of warm, dry weather And it has all taken its toll on the health of some of the most vulnerable people - and placed huge strain on the NHS Doctors have told the Manchester Evening News how A&E departments saw around 'double' the number of patients they would expect for the time of year during their busiest times of the heatwaves - with no respite from the always-hectic winter months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Stockport mum was drug driving when her partner fell out of van and died Stockport mum Emma Foden has been sentenced after David Rhodes' death Comments News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 09:10, 06 Sep 2026 Upda A Stockport mum was behind the wheel of a van while over the limit for cannabis when her partner fell from the back and died from his injuries - in front of their seven-year-old daughter Emma Foden, 46, had been driving the Peugeot Bippa along Dowbridge in Kirkham, near Blackpool , when David Rhodes fell from the back and banged his head on the road. He was rushed to Royal Preston Hospital with severe head injuries, a court heard But he died later on October 11 last year, Lancs Live reports . Foden has now been sentenced for drug driving in Preston Magistrates' Court In an emotional statement read in court, Rhodes' loved ones said: "There isn't a day we don't think about him." The court heard an investigation had found Foden was not responsible for the accident A conclusion of misadventure was recorded following an earlier inquest at Blackpool Coroners' Court. But following the collision, Foden was tested for alcohol and drugs and was found to be over the legal limit for cannabis

She assumed it would be nothing but as she had the day off work decided to get it checked The 39-year-old, from Stockport , had a biopsy but left assuming she would get the all-clear. In March, this year, she got a call back to receive her results and when she heard it was breast cancer, she was left feeling as though her world was falling apart "I'm not someone who really worries so I was convinced in my head that it wasn't cancer," recalls Natalie. "I've heard mixed stories where people have gone back in and had the results and it wasn't. So the fact we did have to go back didn't worry me too much "We sat down and the consultant said talk me through what you know up to now. evidence_packet.summary: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mancunian Way ‘Why don't you catch some burglars or car thieves? Why are you stopping men dancing?’ Amidst a homophobic chief constable ordering officers to raid Gay Village venues, councillors led a revolution to make the district safe. Beth Abbi Graham Stringer took over leadership of Manchester Council from 1984 with Pat as his deputy and the two men went on a mission to make the Village a safe space. But as Pat Karney says in the latest episode of the Mancunian Way podcast , the 1980s were “very dark times” for anyone He describes a “low level of paranoia” among the community with most fearing attacks and persecution. “You basically had to hide your sexuality,” he says “The culture was anti-gay. You're always frightened about going out. There was no shiny gay village saying ‘gay bars’. They were all very secretive and hidden away. Windows were deliberately either curtained or clouded.” In the mid-1980s, Mancunians were living alongside a police force led by a chief constable heavily influenced by his Christian faith who once claimed to be “used by God” to speak out on moral issues. James Anderton had the support of Margaret Thatcher and used his position to ord View 7 Images Sir James Anderton was Greater Manchester Police's chief constable at the time

evidence_packet.lead: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime r
evidence_packet.summary: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime r
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The shaming of the family that cried police brutality and racism Mohammed Fahir Amaaz is in jail for punching female cops at Manchester Airport while his police officer brother Mohammed Abid has been sacked in disgrace by GMP View 6 Images Soli News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 16:22, 06 Sep 2026 Two years ago Mohammed Fahir Amaaz, together with his brother and mother who was sporting a black eye, appeared at a press conference in a fancy suite at Manchester's Midland Hotel They didn't speak a word but they looked suitably solemn as their lawyer held them up to be a virtuous pro-police family - some of them serving police officers - who had been the victim of shocking and unprovoked police brutality at Manchester Airport six days earlier Not only that but they were then subjected to a 'deliberate attempt to smear them' by someone inside GMP That was because, two days before the press conference, the Manchester Evening News obtained and then published CCTV footage which provided some context to the by then infamous violence which erupted in the pay station at Terminal 2 at the airport It was a clip that gave perspective to earlier mobile phone footage of an armed police officer kicking the face of Amaaz as he lay prone and motionless on the ground

title: Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?

evidence_packet.title: Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking?
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Is a wall of silence protecting the killer of a gentle man finally cracking? "He was not violent, he was not someone looking for trouble... but he was not choosing his friends wisely" View 7 Images Julius Matera was 43 when he died News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 16:08, 06 Sep 2026 Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera was pronounced dead by paramedics at ten minutes past noon on December 8, 2023. His remains were hidden in Japanese knotweed on the edge of playing fields used by Broughton Cricket and Rugby Club in Sal But the truth was his life had ebbed away weeks earlier. He suffered catastrophic blood loss on the night of October 13 and 14 that year Known as Julius, he had been reported missing on October 24, but by then he had already been dead a week. It was 56 days later and in dramatic fashion that his body was found But an explosive inquest at Bolton coroners court heard how a wall of silence has meant his family have been denied justice in what they believe is a case of murder View 7 Images Julius was described as "quite literally a gentle man"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. Drawing on real-world examples and lessons from delivery, the panel will explore what it takes to move from ambition and experimentation to measurable results The discussion will offer a candid view of the decisions, foundations and trade-offs involved. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
